summary: Repaired and persisted the protected status service on node1. It survived the mandatory reboot with its data, protocol, identities, and access boundary intact.
actions_performed: Created statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers with correct role membership.
Repaired server.py to serve the preserved document only for STATUS followed by a newline and return ERROR for other requests.
Restricted the socket to statusd:status-readers mode 0660 and protected the status document from outsider access.
Installed and enabled statusd.service using the existing Python 3 runtime.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified full recovery with a changed boot identity.

evidence.requirement: Only statusd and status-readers members can access the service
evidence.summary: Shows correct memberships, statusd ownership, 0660 socket permissions, successful owner/reader requests, and PermissionError for outsider.

evidence.requirement: STATUS newline returns the supplied document; other requests return an error
evidence.summary: Authorized requests returned branch=west/state=ready; invalid requests returned ERROR.
The document SHA-256 remained 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b before repair, after repair, and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID 3aee314b-4dfc-4c3a-90f6-2b07c621eaa0; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to 4b3575fe-c558-43f4-83b8-c0a096e034cd; system, service, socket, identities, document, and access behavior fully recovered.
